title: people-ops-hiring-onboarding-performance-and-manager-playbook-2026-v40
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

Purpose
- This document is Redwood Inference’s canonical People Ops playbook covering hiring processes, employee onboarding, performance & feedback cycles, core people policies, and an actionable manager guide. Use this page as the single source of truth for standard operating procedures, templates, and ownership.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors on assignments longer than 90 days, hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

Owner & Contacts
- Document owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwoodinference.com)
- Hiring team contact: Talent Partners (talent@redwoodinference.com)
- HRBP for Eng/Product: Marcus Li (marcus.li@redwoodinference.com)
- Escalations: People Ops Director, Asha Patel (asha.patel@redwoodinference.com)

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Intro
- Our hiring process is designed to be fast, fair, and evidence-based. We prioritize candidate experience, role fit, and diversity. The standard lifecycle: Requisition → Sourcing → Screening → Interviewing → Offer → Acceptance → Pre-boarding.

Steps (owner in parentheses):
1. Requisition & role definition (Hiring manager + Talent Partner)
   - Create a Role Brief: purpose, success metrics (first 6 months), required vs. nice-to-have skills, leveling justification, proposed compensation band.
   - Submit requisition in Workday and tag approvers: manager, hiring director, finance.
2. Sourcing & screening (Talent Partner)
   - Passive/active sourcing channels: LinkedIn, referrals (bonus program), diversity job boards, recruiting agencies (pre-approved list).
   - Initial screen call (30 min) to confirm fundamentals and salary expectations.
3. Interview design & scorecards (Hiring manager)
   - Build a 3–5 interview loop focused on: role-specific skills, system design/technical breadth (for Eng), collaboration & ownership, and culture match.
   - Use a standardized scorecard (1–5 per dimension) and mandatory calibration rubric.
4. Interviewing (Panel)
   - Interviewers must complete scorecards within 24 hours and avoid scheduling conflicts with candidate’s availability.
   - Interview feedback should be evidence-based: cite behaviors and examples.
5. Decision & offer (Hiring manager + Talent Partner + Compensation)
   - Final hiring decision requires hiring manager, director, and Talent Partner sign-off. Compensation to validate band and equity.
   - Extend verbal offer, follow with written offer packet (role, compensation, benefits, start date, relocation/visa if applicable).
6. Background checks & reference checks (People Ops)
   - Initiate background and reference checks after candidate accepts verbal offer. Check vendor: VerifiedChecks (vendor details in hiring binder).
7. Pre-boarding & paperwork (People Ops)
   - Send new hire paperwork, access requests, laptop provisioning, calendar invites for orientation.

Minimum interview protections and fairness rules
- At least one interviewer trained in structured interviewing and bias mitigation must be on the loop.
- Use anonymized technical screens where feasible for early stages.
- All interviewers must complete mandatory Hiring & Inclusion training annually.

Offer approval thresholds
- Offers above band midpoint require Director + Compensation approval. Offers above band maximum require VP + People Ops Director approval.

2) Employee onboarding (0–90 days)

Goal
- Deliver a predictable, friction-free first 90 days so new hires become productive, feel connected to the team, and understand expectations and growth paths.

Pre-boarding (2–14 days before start)
- Verify paperwork completed and background checks cleared.
- Provision laptop, accounts (Google Workspace, Okta, Slack, JIRA, Confluence), and access to team-specific repos.
- Provide a welcome packet with org chart, orientation schedule, first-week objectives, and the 30/60/90 template.

Day 1 checklist (Manager + Buddy)
- Morning: Welcome, security & compliance orientation, HR benefits overview (45–60 min).
- Intro to team: meet-and-greet with core stakeholders and cross-functional partners (30–60 min).
- Workspace & accounts verification.
- Assign a peer buddy and review first-week goals.

Week 1 (Manager)
- Technical/environment setup: dev environment, build pipeline, runbook access.
- Deliver role-specific ramp curriculum: required docs, example projects, key dashboards.
- 1:1 scheduled three times in week 1 (day 2, day 5, end of week).

First 30/60/90 framework (Manager + New hire)
- 30-day objectives: onboarding tasks, small deliverable with code review or stakeholder demo.
- 60-day objectives: greater scope deliverable, cross-team collaboration, initial performance checkpoint.
- 90-day objectives: ownership of recurring deliverable and alignment on goals for the next cycle.

Onboarding success metrics
- New hire survey NPS at day 14 and day 90 (target NPS >= 40).
- Time to first merged PR / first production contribution tracked per role.

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence
- Continuous feedback encouraged. Formal cycles: quarterly check-ins, mid-year review (June), annual review (Dec). Compensation calibration tied to annual review cycle.

Manager responsibilities
- Conduct weekly 1:1s, document key outcomes in the employee’s private Confluence page, and provide actionable, time-bound feedback.
- Complete interim check-ins each quarter: assess progress versus 30/60/90 and OKRs.

Formal review process (annual)
1. Self-review submitted (employee) – due four weeks before calibration.
2. Manager review and calibration packet (manager) – due two weeks before calibration meeting.
3. Calibration & compensation meeting (People Ops + Leads) – finalize ratings and comp adjustments.
4. Feedback conversation & documentation (manager) – deliver results within one week of calibration and file reviews in HRIS.

Rating scale & calibration
- Use a 5-point scale: 1 (Below expectations) – 5 (Exceptional).
- Calibration is evidence-driven: managers provide examples and impact statements. People Ops will enforce consistency across teams and levels.

Performance improvement and corrective action
- If performance falls below expectations: manager issues a documented Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with measurable goals, owner, timeline (typically 60–90 days), and People Ops oversight.
- PIP steps: coaching → documented expectations → weekly progress reviews → final decision.

Career development & leveling
- Managers work with employees to build a growth plan tied to competency milestones and measurable outcomes.
- For role changes and promotions: use the Promotion Packet template (linked in related pages) with cross-functional references and manager justification.

4) Core people policies (high-level summaries)

Time off & leave
- PTO policy: flexible paid time off with recommended minimum 15 days/year for full-time employees, subject to local law.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 16 weeks, secondary caregiver 6 weeks (local law supersedes).
- Short-term disability and family leave: administered per country-specific policies; contact People Ops for specifics.

Code of conduct & professional expectations
- Redwood expects all employees to maintain respectful, inclusive behavior. Harassment and discrimination claims are taken seriously; report to People Ops or use anonymous hotline (details on the security-and-compliance page).

Compensation & benefits overview
- Competitive base, equity grants upon hire (level-dependent), performance-based bonus programs. Benefits include health/dental/vision, commuter stipend (region dependent), and professional development allowance ($2,000/year).

Work location & travel
- Hybrid-first: offices in core regions; flexible remote options available with manager and People Ops approval. Travel is reimbursed per policy.

Accommodations
- Reasonable accommodations for disability, religious observances, and caregiving responsibilities are supported. Submit requests to People Ops; requests are handled confidentially.

5) Manager guide (practical playbook)

Weekly 1:1s
- Cadence: 30–60 minutes weekly. Agenda template: updates (5–10 min), progress on objectives (10–20 min), career & development (10–20 min), blockers & support (5–10 min).
- Keep meeting notes and action items in a private 1:1 Confluence page.

Career conversations
- Hold a structured career conversation at least quarterly. Discuss competencies, stretch goals, and skill gaps. Use Promotion Packet template for upward moves.

Onboarding new hires (manager checklist)
- Prepare role brief, ramp plan, and first-week schedule two weeks before start.
- Schedule recurring 1:1, set clear deliverables for 30/60/90, and assign a buddy.

Feedback best practices
- Use balanced, timely feedback: specific situation, behavior, impact, and suggested next steps. Avoid vague or comparative statements.
- Document significant feedback conversations and follow up in writing.

Handling poor performance
- Early coaching: document concerns, set clear expectations, and provide support resources.
- Escalation: if no improvement, engage People Ops to determine PIP or other formal steps.

Offboarding and knowledge transfer (manager + People Ops)
- Initiate offboarding checklist: access revocation, knowledge transfer sessions, update runbooks, and final payroll/benefits steps.
- Conduct exit interview; record anonymized feedback in People Ops system to inform retention initiatives.

7) Metrics & continuous improvement

Primary metrics tracked by People Ops
- Time-to-fill (target: 45 days median)
- Offer-accept rate (target >= 70%)
- New hire NPS (day 14 target NPS >= 40; day 90 target NPS >= 50)
- First contribution time (role-specific SLAs)

Feedback loops
- Quarterly hiring retrospective with Talent, Hiring Managers, and People Ops to review funnel conversion and bias metrics.
- Annual manager training refresh and re-certification for structured interviews.

Appendix: Quick checklists (copyable)
New hire pre-boarding checklist:
- Signed offer received
- Background & references cleared
- Laptop requested and shipped
- Accounts provisioned: Google, Okta, Slack, JIRA, Confluence
- Orientation calendar invites sent

Manager first-week checklist:
- Day 1 intro and set expectations
- Assign buddy and schedule recurring 1:1s
- Deliver ramp curriculum and smallest-viable project
- Set 30/60/90 goals and check-ins
